1. Core Clinical Tension: A 60-year-old male presents with an isolated, warm, tender left inguinal mass a decade after completing antimicrobial treatment for a chronic cutaneous-neurological illness. The clinical presentation mimics an acute pyogenic lymphadenitis, incarcerated inguinal hernia, or nodal lymphoma, obscuring a late-onset type 2 lepra reaction (erythema nodosum leprosum, ENL) localized atypically to the inguinal soft tissue.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The breakpoint occurs at initial physical examination and outpatient triage, strictly prior to fine-needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) and special mycobacterial staining.
3. Differential Distinctions: Acute pyogenic lymphadenitis presents with local warmth and erythema, but yields purulence with bacterial organisms on Gram stain and culture. Nodal lymphoma presents with non-tender or progressively enlarging lymphadenopathy lacking neutrophilic and foamy histiocytic inflammation.
case_prompt:
A 60-year-old male presented to the outpatient clinic with localized pain, tenderness, and progressive swelling in the left inguinal region. His medical history was notable for completion of a course of multidrug therapy 10 years earlier for a chronic dermatologic and peripheral nerve disorder; he had remained symptom-free in the interim.

On physical examination, vital signs were stable. In the left inguinal region, palpation revealed a solitary, tender, diffuse swelling measuring 3.0 cm × 1.5 cm. The overlying skin was distinctly warm to the touch. No other cutaneous ulcers, visible fistulae, or generalized peripheral lymphadenopathies were noted on initial physical evaluation.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered due to the localized tenderness, warmth, and acute nodal swelling, but Gram stain and bacterial cultures showed no bacterial organisms, and cytology demonstrated a chronic histiocytic and granulomatous background rather than simple suppurative pyogenic infection.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: On clinical examination, a tender diffuse swelling measuring 3 x 1.5 cm the in left inguinal region was palpated. Skin over the swelling was warm. FNAC was performed and both air-dried and alcohol-fixed smears were prepared.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Incarcerated inguinal hernia or soft tissue neoplasm
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Considered as an anatomical or neoplastic groin mass, but excluded by cytological demonstration of active inflammatory infiltrate containing neutrophils, foamy macrophages, histiocytes, and multinucleated giant cells.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: The Wright-Giemsa (WG) stained smears showed lymphoid cells along with degenerated and intact neutrophils, clusters of foamy macrophages, histiocytes, and giant cells in a hemorrhagic background.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Fine-needle aspiration demonstrating negative images of bacilli on Wright-Giemsa smears and numerous intracellular and extracellular acid-fast lepra bacilli on modified Fite staining confirmed erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL) presenting as an isolated inguinal mass.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Occasional shadows of negative images of bacilli were seen. In view of clinical and cytological findings, Fite stain for lepra bacilli was performed, which showed numerous intracellular and extracellular lepra bacilli [Figure 1].

editor_comments: This case highlights an uncommon presentation of erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL, Type 2 lepra reaction) presenting as an isolated, tender inguinal pseudo-mass a decade after completing multidrug therapy (MDT), successfully diagnosed via fine-needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) with Fite stain.
